verdict.rationale: Adyen's marketing page names a 'Risk Rule Backtesting' capability that tests risk rules against historical data before going live, so the product itself claims the core of this story. The claim is a single thin marketing line with no technical docs or hands-on corroboration. Risk experiments (A/B testing profiles on live traffic) are a different capability from historical backtesting and are not credited here. Missing for 10: documentation of backtest outputs showing what would have been blocked vs. flagged/reviewed, cost or impact estimates, the backtesting workflow in technical docs, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a risk analyst, I can backtest a rule against my historical traffic before deploying it, seeing exactly what it would have blocked, flagged, and cost

citations.quote: Risk Rule Backtesting. Test and optimize risk rules against historical data before going live.
